question.problem:
In a particular region, the heights of adult males are normally distributed with mean $70\,\text{in}$ and standard deviation $4\,\text{in}.$ In the same region, the heights of adult females are normally distributed with mean $65\,\text{in}$ and standard deviation $3.5\,\text{in}.$ If one woman and one man are randomly selected, what is the probability that the woman is taller than the man? You may assume that the heights of males and females are independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.9\,$ | $\,0.1841\,$ | $\,0.1814\,$ | $\,0.1788\,$ | $\,0.1762\,$ | $\,0.1736\,$ |
| $\,-0.8\,$ | $\,0.2119\,$ | $\,0.2090\,$ | $\,0.2061\,$ | $\,0.2033\,$ | $\,0.2005\,$ |
| $\,-0.7\,$ | $\,0.2420\,$ | $\,0.2389\,$ | $\,0.2358\,$ | $\,0.2327\,$ | $\,0.2296\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ denote the height of an adult male, and let $Y$ denote the height of an adult female. We want to find 

$$
P(X<Y)=P(X-Y<0).
$$

Since $X$ and $Y$ are independent random variables such that $X∼N(70,{4}^{2})$ and $Y∼N(65,{3.5}^{2})$, then 

$$
\begin{aligned}X-Y & ∼N(70-65,{4}^{2}+{3.5}^{2}) \\  & ∼N(5,28.25).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variable $X-Y$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu =5$ and standard deviation $\sigma =\sqrt{28.25}.$

To find $P(X-Y<0),$ we convert $X-Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X-Y<0) & =P(Z<\frac{0-5}{\sqrt{28.25}}) \\  & ≈P(Z<-0.94) \\  & =P(Z\le -0.94) \\  & =Φ(-0.94)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(-0.94)≈0.1736.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X-Y<0) & ≈Φ(-0.94) \\  & ≈0.1736.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that the probability that a woman is taller than a man is $0.1736.$
